title: KMC bulldozer clears shed outside Abhishek Banerjee's home; he goes to Election Commission
dek: The civic body removed a security shed and gate from the footpath at Kalighat. Abhishek alleges intimidation linked to the Trinamool symbol case; a minister says neighbours had suffered. The High Court reserved its order on his security.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) workers, backed by police and central forces, used a bulldozer on Thursday morning to remove a tin-roofed shed and an iron gate from the footpath outside Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee's home at Kalighat. Hours later, Mr Banerjee complained to the Election Commission of India (ECI) that he was being intimidated, and the Calcutta High Court reserved its order on his challenge to the cut in his security cover.

The removal at 121 Kalighat Road began late on Wednesday and was finished on Thursday morning, according to reports. CCTV cameras mounted on public poles were also taken down, reports said. Former chief minister Mamata Banerjee later went to the house and protested there with her nephew.

## The civic body's case

The KMC served a notice on Wednesday and acted on a request from the Assistant Commissioner of Police of Kolkata Police's South Division to clear the footpath for pedestrians, according to reports. The notice said the structure had been built long ago for the security staff of a VVIP and was still in use by security personnel, reports said. The KMC has not published the notice.

State Panchayat and Rural Development Minister Dilip Ghosh of the BJP said the action "is justified as people in the neighbourhood were facing lots of hardships", and that Mr Banerjee "used to consider himself as being above the law", according to reports.

## Trinamool's response

Trinamool spokesperson Arka Nag said the shed had been built by the state's Directorate of Security for the police guarding Mr Banerjee when he had Z-plus cover. "The shed was constructed by the police," he said. The party said Mr Banerjee's office staff had begun dismantling it themselves on Wednesday evening.

In a post on X, Mr Banerjee, the MP for Diamond Harbour, wrote: "No number of bulldozers can silence my voice or break my resolve." He said he would not retreat in his fight against those he called "Bangla Birodhis" (enemies of Bengal).

His complaint to the ECI, quoted in reports, alleges that "a group of persons launched an attack upon his residence-cum-office" on the night of 6-7 November and that there were "similar acts of surveillance and reconnaissance" on 10 and 11 November. It says a police-installed security gate was demolished "in the early hours of 12th November, 2026", and alleges that BJP-linked people, "allegedly acting with the support, assistance or connivance of certain police personnel", may try to take documents prepared for the dispute over the Trinamool name and symbol, which is pending before the Commission. It asks the ECI to order that those papers be protected. These are allegations; the police and the BJP have not responded to them in detail.

## In the High Court

Also on Thursday, Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court reserved his order on Mr Banerjee's petition against the reduction of his security from Z-plus, which he had held since 2013, to X category on 11 May 2026, two days after the BJP government took office. The state told the court there was no threat to him and that its review committee would meet again later this month, according to reports. The judge asked why no review had been held in six months.

Mr Banerjee's counsel, Shoaib Alam, alleged that 40 to 50 people with sticks had attacked the house at 2 am on his birthday, one of six attacks he said had taken place.

## Minister says Banerjee was not targeted

On Friday Dilip Ghosh said the drive was part of a wider campaign against encroachments and that Mr Banerjee had not been singled out. "Any form of illegal encroachment is being removed," he told reporters in Kolkata, adding that the city was short of roads and footpaths and that illegal structures were being demolished in many places. Mr Banerjee said he would not be deterred by what he called "bulldozer politics", according to reports.

## Contempt request in the High Court

Reports of Thursday's High Court hearing, published on Friday, gave more detail of the exchanges. The state's Additional Advocate General, Billwadal Bhattacharya, submitted a video and transcript of remarks Mr Banerjee made at his birthday gathering on 7 November, in which he reportedly said a section of the judiciary was a "mute spectator", and asked the court to begin contempt proceedings on its own. Mr Alam opposed this, arguing the remarks had nothing to do with the security relief sought. Justice Rao said the controversy would not affect how the security petition was decided, according to reports. The request is not a finding that Mr Banerjee committed contempt.

The state also argued that no one can claim a particular category of security as a right and that most MPs have X category cover. For the Centre, Additional Solicitor General Dhiraj Trivedi said Mr Banerjee had been discharged from hospital without injuries after some of the incidents he cited. The judge asked whether anything had stopped the state's review committee from meeting before its six-monthly review, given the incidents reported since May.

## Background

Trinamool and BJP supporters clashed outside the house during the night of 6-7 November, Mr Banerjee's 39th birthday, and police used batons to disperse them. The ECI froze the All India Trinamool Congress name and symbol on 17 September after the party split, and the Supreme Court has given the Commission four months from 28 September to decide which faction gets them.

## What happens next

The High Court's order on his security is awaited, as is any response from the ECI to his complaint. The state has said its next routine security review is due at the end of November. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has since said he will appoint ward coordinators in Kolkata and Howrah from 1 December if civic elections are not held.
